sections.presenting_complaint: Red, swollen left shin since Wednesday morning.
sections.history: Scratched by a rose bush while gardening on Tuesday; redness from Wednesday morning (patient initially said Tuesday). Warm and sore. No blistering or dark patches. Temperature 37.6 °C this morning (self-measured). Systemically well; no rigors, vomiting or confusion. No swelling of the other leg. Type 2 diabetes. Lives alone; daughter visits daily.
sections.medications_allergies: Metformin 500 mg twice daily. Allergic to penicillin.
sections.examination: Warm and tender on palpation; no crepitus. Erythema over the anterior right shin, approximately 10 cm across, with a small central scratch. No blistering or necrosis visible.
sections.impression: Cellulitis of the left lower leg (Eron class I) following a scratch.
sections.plan: Flucloxacillin 500 mg four times daily for 7 days, on an empty stomach. Margin of erythema marked with pen. Elevation and paracetamol. Photo or video review in 48 hours.
sections.safety_netting: Same-day contact (or 111) if spreading beyond the marked line, high fever, rigors, feeling very unwell or confused, or rapidly worsening pain. Call 999 if very unwell.
